findings.where: Foreground sofa, x 194-2095, y 1348-1600. Left arm outline x 198-402, y 1355-1570. Right arm x 1790-2095, y 1350-1600.
findings.what: The wood grain is gone, but the new sofa does not read as upholstery. At 5x the back rail shows soft, cloud-like blotches and no weave, nap or fuzz at its edge. The arms look like smooth, crumpled rubber tubes, each with a dark crease folded into it. The outline is faceted. Tracing the left arm's outer edge, it runs in straight lines between kinks: exactly 2 px of x per 5 rows from y 1505 to 1565, 4 px per 5 rows from y 1460 to 1475, and 6 to 9 px per 5 rows above that. The sofa is the nearest object and fills the bottom sixth of the frame. At 1300 px it reads as a soft dark sofa, but more like smooth leather or clay than fabric. At full size the facets and blotches read as CG.
findings.expected: Upholstery with a visible weave or nap and a soft fabric edge, and an outline with no straight runs. Failing that, a lower crop that keeps only the back rail.

findings.where: Record sleeves leaning against the foot of the credenza, x 1375-1556, y 1130-1290
findings.what: The front sleeve carries a flat, saturated green stepped shape on white. The sleeve behind it has a column of alternating orange and blue squares along its edge. There is no lettering, but it reads as an invented placeholder graphic. The green is as flat as the painted wall (std 0.93 levels; the wall is 0.79), with no paper texture, sheen or falloff over its 140 px height. It is the only saturated non-red color in the frame: every pixel with C* over 40 and a green hue lies inside this stack. It is also the complement of Ember, so at 1300 px it is the first thing after the two speakers that pulls the eye, about 100 px from the right Tropos. The stack has no contact line at the floor either: the oak just below the white sleeve reads L* 65-69, brighter than the oak beside it at L* 49-53.
findings.expected: Sleeves that do not compete with the tint: muted or dark, or turned to show plain backs or spines. They should show card texture and a thin contact shadow where they stand on the oak.

findings.where: Mantle tonearm pillar and arm rest, x 1296-1316, y 893-914
findings.what: The arm pillar and the arm rest read as bright polished metal: L* 67-74 across the pillar, with a clipped line at L* 100. The studio Mantle's pillar is satin black (L* 1-5 in ember.png). The arm tube and counterweight are black. The first version looked the same. At 1300 px this is a small bright tick to the right of the record. At full size it reads as chrome, not the satin black Rega arm. This is separate from the known question about the deck. The product lens should decide whether it misstates the product.
findings.expected: A satin black pillar and rest, as in ember.png, with at most a narrow line of sheen.

findings.where: Dark card sleeves behind the Mantle, x 963-1228, y 800-938
findings.what: The two blank sleeves are perfectly flat (high-pass std 0.38-0.39, the same as the painted wall). Their tone (L* 26-28) equals the left half of the deck top (L* 28.6), so the deck's back edge disappears into them. Past their right edge (x 1228) the polished deck mirrors the wall instead (L* 59-66), so the deck reads dark on the left and gray on the right. This adds to the known deck question rather than being a separate fault.
findings.expected: If the sleeves stay: card texture, a lit top edge, and their right edge kept clear of the deck so the deck reads as one tone.
